title: The Fate of the Nail
text: “It seems he’s been in touch with his family back home. Since there are various things they need to discuss and he needs to undergo a complete course of treatment, he’s over there getting a thorough medical examination.”
“Since the honor of the Warbart family has been tarnished, plans are being drawn up to take secret yet certain revenge against Takt’s faction.”
“That’s my job.”
“I’m well aware of that. Lord Magalum also seemed to be struggling to explain that part.”
“Wolf’s family, huh… They’ve been eagerly inviting me to visit next time—I wonder if it’ll be okay?”
“It should be fine since Lord Magalum is there. In his prime, Lord Magalum was even more formidable than Lord Ruhabart and possessed the skill to prevent strange power brokers from meddling.”
“Is he actually the intellectual type?”
“Not quite to that extent, but he has enough power to keep his clan in line. Above all, since he’s been newly appointed as the Hero of the Claw, no one can defy him.”
It is Filo-tan’s Claw, after all… but I suppose it might be better than having it snatched away by a Rival.
“The Claw is Filo-tan’s weapon. We should discuss this thoroughly later to ensure it ends up in Filo-tan’s hands.”
“Motoyasu-kun, you’re still the same as ever.”

By the way, the Claw never made its way from Wolf’s hands to Filo-tan’s. It’s a real pain. It keeps falling into the hands of Rival teams or changing hands constantly depending on the situation—it’s way too unstable.

“Incidentally, while I don’t know the full truth, the Warbart family is also known as a bloodline that swore loyalty to the first Shield Hero. That makes them a bloodline of retainers to the Shield Hero—separate from Lord Liberacion’s Lizardman lineage.”
“Wow… somehow, all the slaves I’ve met in Melromarc seem really amazing—though I guess Raphtalia and Theo are different. Maybe Theo comes from an impressive lineage too.”
I wonder about Big Sister? Unfortunately, I don’t know much about that, but since her village was a place that suffered damage from the waves, there might be a story there in its own right.

“In any case, Wolf—who, as the ‘Mad Dog,’ only ever opened up to the Shield Hero and a select few… Now that Lord Magalum has regained his sanity, his work from here on out should be a lot easier, don’t you think?”
Elephant’s lines sound like something from the circus.

“Well, he used to serve as a sparring partner for Motoyasu’s performances, but I wonder if he’ll be easier to control now? Maybe Elmelo would feel more reassured if he received some support from Wolf’s family?”
“P-please don’t worry about me—really… they’re just a hopeless bunch.”

Elephant is quite humble, isn’t he? I’d like those pigs—including Takt—to take a cue from him. Well, even the pigs in the world I used to know managed to get by just fine by relying on emotional appeals and shouting, “Just do your best!” It’s no good to dither and worry when you can handle things with just that much effort.
“Elephant, strength solves everything. It’s all about power!”
“Motoyasu-kun, isn’t that something a villain would say? You’ll end up just like that Takt guy.”

“That’s not true. What Takt represents is violence—power without justice—whereas Elephant’s power is the power of justice. Justice without power is powerless. I don’t think it’s right to just keep getting beaten up without fighting back.”
“Eh…”

The Elephant may not be able to phrase this very well, but this is the truth. Ark and Hou-kun said so, too. That being able to fight for someone else is a noble and important thing. Takt’s power is for his own sake, which is why it’s no good. The Elephant wields his power for those he respects and those aligned with them, so it is justice.
“How should I put it… Motoyasu-kun, you’re sometimes more level-headed than I’d imagine.”
“That’s a bit embarrassing.”
“Am I being complimented…?”
Elephant and the envoy from Siltvelt are giving wry smiles, but I didn’t mean to say anything strange.
“To summarize, will Wolf be reuniting with his Father after his thorough medical examination?”

“Yeah. Since the official line is that he’ll be working with me in secret in Melromarc as the ‘Claw Hero,’ it seems that’ll help defuse some of the war-like tension in Siltvelt to a certain extent.　I actually thought it might shift the mood toward an offensive, though.”
“They’ve been acting rationally from the start, after all. The PR effect of ‘protecting the people of the Seaetto territories’ is having a major impact.”

They’re avoiding good deeds as much as possible, after all. For the most part, support within Melromarc is concentrated on Ren and Itsuki. Word has it that Rafumi is acting as a stand-in, resolving various issues more smoothly than Ren could. On the other hand, Itsuki seems to be carrying out reforms that benefit corrupt nobles, much like in the loop where he remained in the original world or in Melromarc. We’re seeing a natural trend where support is gathering around Ren, who is acting as the stand-in.
“Well, as a result, our military strength is definitely coming together… I just hope things can be settled peacefully.”

So, it seems the situation with Wolf’s grudge has settled down to some extent. Of course, Takt dealt with him in a brutal manner and showed it to Wolf. He still hasn’t suffered enough! Next up is the Crimson Swine! How should I torment and finish him off? Turning him into a second meat block is one option! Timing is key. If I’m not careful, it could trigger Trash’s rampage, so I’ll just have to wait and see how things play out.
And so, this is our daily life as we deal with the issues between Takt and Wolf.

“Ah… I remember that everyone stuck by me even when I’d lost my sense of self. I’ve regained my memories and all sorts of things. My name is Magalum, but I’d like you to keep calling me Wolf here, just as you always have. I look forward to working with you all from now on.”
It seems Wolf has returned and reintroduced himself to everyone. This happened at the circus camp in Melromarc.
“Huh… I’d heard rumors, but this is a surprise.”
“Yeah, you’re right.”
Panda’s adoptive father and grandfather had been feeding Wolf and training him, so they were already somewhat familiar with him.
“I didn’t know a thing about it.”
Panda was completely left out of the loop.
“Nice to meet you all again.”
“Nice to meet you too… You were one of the first companions to serve as a slave under the Shield Hero, so I suppose you’re the oldest here?”
The Rabbit Man and the Crocodile Man each introduced themselves to Wolf all over again.
“Ah… Now that I’ve regained my sense of self, I’d like to ask for your continued support.”
And with that, Wolf greeted the Crocodile Man and the Rabbit Man. They seem quite close—it feels like he trusts them almost as much as he trusts his Father.
“I believe you became the Claw Hero, right? The events back then were truly dramatic.”
“Theodore… you really love stories, don’t you?”
“Yes.”
“I used to aspire to that, too. My older brother became a Hero, and as his squire, I honed my skills alongside him and handled negotiations on behalf of my clumsy brother.”
“Are you two kindred spirits?”
“We were, originally.”
The Rabbit Man and Wolf shook hands. Then, Wolf turned his gaze toward the Crocodile Man.

“I’ve heard it in the legends. You’re a descendant of the Lizardman who served as the first Shield Hero’s squire—we have such legends here as well. From now on, let’s join forces and pledge our loyalty to Lord Naofumi, the Shield Hero.”
“Ah… I have no intention of losing when it comes to loyalty. Not even to the Seven Star Heroes.”
“Of course. I’m grateful for this fate. No matter what it takes, I’ll become a great hero who surpasses my older brother.”

Tsumé seems to have made up his mind about something, but as for me, I want to possess Filo-tan. Hey, Tsumé! I ordered you to possess Filo-tan. I secretly ordered him to be stripped of his status as a familiar, but Tsumé didn’t budge at all. Just like when he possessed my Rival, he’s a stubborn little claw. Maybe I’ll ask Ark again if he comes to visit us?
